title: The Fear of the Lord
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The fear of the Lord is reverent awe, humble worship, holy seriousness, and obedient trust before God. It is not sinful terror for those in Christ, but the right response to God’s holiness, authority, glory, and mercy.
summary: The fear of the Lord is reverent awe, humble worship, holy seriousness, and obedient trust before God. It is not sinful terror for those in Christ, but the right response to God’s holiness, authority, glory, and mercy.
christFocus: Jesus Christ teaches believers whom to fear and brings them into reverent confidence before God. Through Him, fear of condemnation is answered, while holy reverence is deepened.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge and wisdom. It means seeing God as He is and responding with reverence, humility, worship, and obedience.

This fear is not the same as running from God in unbelieving terror. For believers, Christ removes condemnation. Yet grace does not make God casual. Those who know His mercy should still tremble at His Word and honor His holiness.

Scripture connects the fear of the Lord with obedience. The whole duty of man is to fear God and keep His commandments. Reverence that never obeys is not biblical fear.

The early church walked in the fear of the Lord and the comfort of the Holy Spirit. Healthy Christian life includes both reverence and comfort, seriousness and joy, humility and confidence.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people either fear everything except God or treat God with little reverence. Both distort life. When God is not rightly feared, sin becomes lighter, people become larger, and wisdom is lost.

This doctrine frees believers from the fear of man. Those who reverence God rightly do not need to be ruled by approval, rejection, threats, or shame.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Cultivate reverence before God. Let His holiness, judgment, mercy, and glory shape how you speak, worship, decide, repent, and obey. Do not live in condemnation if you are in Christ, but do not lose the holy seriousness of belonging to the Lord.
